title: Stalk of the etale inverse image of a sheaf of sets, with germs
statement: Let $e:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $G$ a sheaf of sets on $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Let $e^{-1}G$ be its etale inverse image (a sheaf of sets on $T_{\Et}$) and, for an object $U$ of $S_{\Et}$ and $a\in G(U)$, let $e^*a\in(e^{-1}G)(U\times_ST)$ be the image of $a$ under the unit $G\to e_*e^{-1}G$, both as in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. Let $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] and $\bar s=e\circ\bar t$; stalks, pointed etale neighbourhoods and germs are those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. For a pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar s$, the pair $(U\times_ST,(\bar u,\bar t))$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar t$. Then there is exactly one map of sets $c_{e,\bar t,G}:(e^{-1}G)_{\bar t}\to G_{\bar s}$ such that for every pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar s$ and every $a\in G(U)$\n$$c_{e,\bar t,G}\bigl(\text{germ of }e^*a\text{ at }(U\times_ST,(\bar u,\bar t))\bigr)=\text{germ of }a\text{ at }(U,\bar u),$$\nand $c_{e,\bar t,G}$ is bijective.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback) (3), for sheaves of sets, with the compatibility with germs of pulled-back sections made explicit (the abelian version is lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ)

proof.text: *Notation; the model of $e^{-1}$ and its unit.* Let $b:S_{\Et}\to T_{\Et}$, $U\mapsto U\times_ST$, $g\mapsto g\times\mathrm{id}_T$, be the base-change functor, with projections $p_U:U\times_ST\to U$, $q_U:U\times_ST\to T$; $U\times_ST\to T$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (1). For an object $V$ of $T_{\Et}$ let $\mathcal I_V$ be the category of pairs $(U,\varphi)$, $U\in S_{\Et}$, $\varphi:V\to U\times_ST$ a morphism of $T_{\Et}$, a morphism $(U,\varphi)\to(U',\varphi')$ being $g:U\to U'$ in $S_{\Et}$ with $(g\times\mathrm{id})\circ\varphi=\varphi'$. As in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], $e_pG(V)=\varinjlim_{(U,\varphi)\in\mathcal I_V^{\mathrm{op}}}G(U)$ (colimit of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]) with coprojections $\iota_{(U,\varphi)}:G(U)\to e_pG(V)$; the transition relations are $\iota_{(U,\varphi)}(G(g)a')=\iota_{(U',\varphi')}(a')$ for $g:(U,\varphi)\to(U',\varphi')$, and the restriction along $h:V'\to V$ satisfies $e_pG(h)\circ\iota_{(U,\varphi)}=\iota_{(U,\varphi\circ h)}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-sets-left-exact] (1) (with $\mathcal C=S_{\Et}$, $\mathcal D=T_{\Et}$, $b$ as above) $e_p\dashv e^p$, $e^p\mathcal H=\mathcal H\circ b$, with unit $G(U)\to e_pG(U\times_ST)$ the coprojection $\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}$. Further $e^{-1}G=(e_pG)^\#$ with canonical map $\theta:e_pG\to e^{-1}G$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] (2) (values in sets, $u=b$) the adjunction $e^{-1}\dashv e_*$, $e_*=e^p$ on sheaves, is the composite of $e_p\dashv e^p$ and $\#\dashv$ (inclusion). The unit of a composite of adjunctions is the composite of the units, so the unit $G\to e_*e^{-1}G$ at $U$ is $\theta_{U\times_ST}\circ\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}$, i.e. $e^*a=\theta_{U\times_ST}(\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}(a))$ for $a\in G(U)$.

source.place: equation (equation-pullback) before Lemma Tag 03Q1; sites.tex Tags 00VD, 00VE (the unit is $c(\mathrm{id}_{u(U)})$) and 00WX

proof.text: *Elements of a colimit of sets come from the coprojections.* Let $(L,(\iota_i)_{i\in I})$ be a colimit of a diagram $D$ of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and $L'=\bigcup_i\iota_i(D(i))\subseteq L$. The maps $\chi,\mathbf 1:L\to\{0,1\}$, $\chi$ the indicator of $L'$ and $\mathbf 1$ constant, both satisfy $\chi\circ\iota_i=\mathbf 1\circ\iota_i$ (constant $1$) for all $i$, so by the uniqueness in the universal property $\chi=\mathbf 1$, i.e. $L'=L$. Consequently two maps of sets out of $L$ that agree on every $\iota_i(x)$ are equal. This is used for the stalks $G_{\bar s}$, $(e_pG)_{\bar t}$ and for the sets $e_pG(V)$.

*Reduction to the presheaf pullback.* Write $(e_pG)_{\bar t}=\varinjlim_{(V,\bar v)\in\mathcal N_{\bar t}^{\mathrm{op}}}e_pG(V)$ for the stalk of the presheaf of sets $e_pG$, $\mathcal N_{\bar t}$ the pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar t$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], and $[x]_{(V,\bar v)}$ for the class of $x\in e_pG(V)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheafification-geometric-stalk] (for $\mathcal F=e_pG$ on $T_{\Et}$) the map $\theta_{\bar t}:(e_pG)_{\bar t}\to(e^{-1}G)_{\bar t}$, $[x]_{(V,\bar v)}\mapsto$ germ of $\theta_V(x)$ at $(V,\bar v)$, is bijective, $(e^{-1}G)_{\bar t}$ being the stalk of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. So it suffices to build a bijection $\beta:(e_pG)_{\bar t}\to G_{\bar s}$ and put $c=\beta\circ\theta_{\bar t}^{-1}$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 03Q1 (3): 'by Lemma 03PT taking stalks commutes with sheafification'

proof.text: *The map $\alpha:G_{\bar s}\to(e_pG)_{\bar t}$.* For a pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar s$ ($(U\to S)\circ\bar u=\bar s=e\circ\bar t$) the morphism $(\bar u,\bar t):\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U\times_ST$ is defined [def-pc-fibre-product] and $q_U\circ(\bar u,\bar t)=\bar t$, so $(U\times_ST,(\bar u,\bar t))\in\mathcal N_{\bar t}$ (step 0: $U\times_ST\to T$ is etale); this is the claim in the statement. Let $\alpha_{(U,\bar u)}:G(U)\to(e_pG)_{\bar t}$, $a\mapsto[\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}(a)]_{(U\times_ST,(\bar u,\bar t))}$. Compatibility: for a morphism $h:(U',\bar u')\to(U,\bar u)$ of $\mathcal N_{\bar s}$ ($h\bar u'=\bar u$) and $a\in G(U)$, $h\times\mathrm{id}:(U'\times_ST,(\bar u',\bar t))\to(U\times_ST,(\bar u,\bar t))$ is a morphism of $\mathcal N_{\bar t}$ since $(h\times\mathrm{id})\circ(\bar u',\bar t)=(h\bar u',\bar t)=(\bar u,\bar t)$; hence $[\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}(a)]_{(U\times_ST,(\bar u,\bar t))}=[e_pG(h\times\mathrm{id})\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}(a)]_{(U'\times_ST,(\bar u',\bar t))}=[\iota_{(U,h\times\mathrm{id})}(a)]_{(U'\times_ST,(\bar u',\bar t))}$, and $h:(U',\mathrm{id})\to(U,h\times\mathrm{id})$ is a morphism of $\mathcal I_{U'\times_ST}$, so $\iota_{(U,h\times\mathrm{id})}(a)=\iota_{(U',\mathrm{id})}(G(h)a)$. Thus $\alpha_{(U',\bar u')}\circ G(h)=\alpha_{(U,\bar u)}$, and by the universal property of $G_{\bar s}=\varinjlim_{\mathcal N_{\bar s}^{\mathrm{op}}}G(U)$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] there is a unique map $\alpha$ with $\alpha([a]_{(U,\bar u)})=[\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}(a)]_{(U\times_ST,(\bar u,\bar t))}$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 03Q1 (3), the chain of equalities of colimits

proof.text: *The map $\beta:(e_pG)_{\bar t}\to G_{\bar s}$.* Fix $(V,\bar v)\in\mathcal N_{\bar t}$. For $(U,\varphi)\in\mathcal I_V$ put $\bar u_\varphi=p_U\circ\varphi\circ\bar v$; then $(U\to S)\circ\bar u_\varphi=e\circ q_U\circ\varphi\circ\bar v=e\circ(V\to T)\circ\bar v=e\circ\bar t=\bar s$ ($\varphi$ is a $T$-morphism), so $(U,\bar u_\varphi)\in\mathcal N_{\bar s}$. The maps $G(U)\to G_{\bar s}$, $a\mapsto[a]_{(U,\bar u_\varphi)}$, are compatible over $\mathcal I_V^{\mathrm{op}}$: for $g:(U,\varphi)\to(U',\varphi')$, $g\bar u_\varphi=g\,p_U\varphi\bar v=p_{U'}(g\times\mathrm{id})\varphi\bar v=p_{U'}\varphi'\bar v=\bar u_{\varphi'}$, so $g$ is a morphism $(U,\bar u_\varphi)\to(U',\bar u_{\varphi'})$ of $\mathcal N_{\bar s}$ and $[G(g)a']_{(U,\bar u_\varphi)}=[a']_{(U',\bar u_{\varphi'})}$. By the universal property of $e_pG(V)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] they induce $\beta_{(V,\bar v)}:e_pG(V)\to G_{\bar s}$ with $\beta_{(V,\bar v)}(\iota_{(U,\varphi)}(a))=[a]_{(U,p_U\varphi\bar v)}$. These are compatible over $\mathcal N_{\bar t}^{\mathrm{op}}$: for $h:(V',\bar v')\to(V,\bar v)$ ($h\bar v'=\bar v$), $\beta_{(V',\bar v')}(e_pG(h)\iota_{(U,\varphi)}(a))=\beta_{(V',\bar v')}(\iota_{(U,\varphi h)}(a))=[a]_{(U,p_U\varphi h\bar v')}=[a]_{(U,p_U\varphi\bar v)}=\beta_{(V,\bar v)}(\iota_{(U,\varphi)}(a))$, and two maps out of $e_pG(V)$ agreeing on all $\iota_{(U,\varphi)}(a)$ are equal (step 1). So there is a unique map $\beta$ with $\beta([\iota_{(U,\varphi)}(a)]_{(V,\bar v)})=[a]_{(U,p_U\circ\varphi\circ\bar v)}$: the correspondence of the source, the pair $(V,\bar v)$, $\varphi$ going to the pointed neighbourhood $(U,p_U\varphi\bar v)$ of $\bar s$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 03Q1 (3): 'the pair $(U,\overline u)$ and the map $a:U\to X\times_YV$ corresponds to the pair $(V,a\circ\overline u)$'

proof.text: *$\alpha$ and $\beta$ are mutually inverse* (explicit inverse maps in place of the cofinality argument of the source; no filteredness is used). By step 1 every element of $G_{\bar s}$ is some $[a]_{(U,\bar u)}$ and every element of $(e_pG)_{\bar t}$ is some $[\iota_{(U,\varphi)}(a)]_{(V,\bar v)}$ (step 1 applied to the stalk and then to $e_pG(V)$), so it suffices to check on these. (i) $\beta\alpha([a]_{(U,\bar u)})=\beta([\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}(a)]_{(U\times_ST,(\bar u,\bar t))})=[a]_{(U,p_U\circ(\bar u,\bar t))}=[a]_{(U,\bar u)}$. (ii) Put $\bar u=p_U\varphi\bar v$; then $\alpha\beta([\iota_{(U,\varphi)}(a)]_{(V,\bar v)})=[\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}(a)]_{(U\times_ST,(\bar u,\bar t))}$. The $T$-morphism $\varphi$ satisfies $p_U\varphi\bar v=\bar u$ and $q_U\varphi\bar v=(V\to T)\bar v=\bar t$, so $\varphi\circ\bar v=(\bar u,\bar t)$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and $\varphi:(V,\bar v)\to(U\times_ST,(\bar u,\bar t))$ is a morphism of $\mathcal N_{\bar t}$. Hence $[\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}(a)]_{(U\times_ST,(\bar u,\bar t))}=[e_pG(\varphi)\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}(a)]_{(V,\bar v)}=[\iota_{(U,\varphi)}(a)]_{(V,\bar v)}$. So $\beta$ is bijective with inverse $\alpha$.

*Existence, germ formula, bijectivity and uniqueness of $c$.* Put $c_{e,\bar t,G}=\beta\circ\theta_{\bar t}^{-1}:(e^{-1}G)_{\bar t}\to G_{\bar s}$, bijective by steps 2 and 5. For $(U,\bar u)\in\mathcal N_{\bar s}$ and $a\in G(U)$, by step 0 the germ of $e^*a=\theta_{U\times_ST}(\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}(a))$ at $(U\times_ST,(\bar u,\bar t))$ is $\theta_{\bar t}([\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}(a)]_{(U\times_ST,(\bar u,\bar t))})=\theta_{\bar t}(\alpha([a]_{(U,\bar u)}))$, so $c$ sends it to $\beta\alpha([a]_{(U,\bar u)})=[a]_{(U,\bar u)}$, the germ of $a$ at $(U,\bar u)$: the germ formula holds. Uniqueness: $\theta_{\bar t}\circ\alpha$ is bijective (steps 2, 5) and every element of $G_{\bar s}$ is a germ $[a]_{(U,\bar u)}$ (step 1), so every element of $(e^{-1}G)_{\bar t}$ is the germ of some $e^*a$ at some $(U\times_ST,(\bar u,\bar t))$; a map satisfying the germ formula is prescribed on all of these, hence equals $c_{e,\bar t,G}$.
